settings.name_in_paper: Coverage-indicator subset selection with bandit feedback
unmapped: Reward on round t is the indicator that the chosen set (|C_t| <= m) intersects an adversarially chosen set A_t (max-of-coverage / sum-max submodular reward)
Only the scalar reward r_t(C_t) is observed
Guarantee is an approximation-ratio (alpha-)regret with ratio 1-((|S|-1)/|S|)^m against any comparator set S of arbitrary size
Learner knows the action size m

algorithms.name: Hedge/Exp3-style algorithm with m i.i.d. draws from a distribution over items

conditions: comparator S is any subset of [K] (any size)
approximation factor (1-((|S|-1)/|S|)^m) applied to comparator reward
results.notes: Bound is on alpha-regret: (1-((|S|-1)/|S|)^m) * sum_t r_t(S) - E[sum_t r_t(C_t)] <= sqrt(2 ln K m (K+m-1) T). K = number of items (paper's nid), m = max set size. Quantity set to 'other' since it is approximation regret. Draft paper; Theorem 5.1 (conditional hardness of improving the approximation factor, via set cover reduction) and Theorem 9.4 (generalisation to pseudo-concave partial-submodular rewards, stated with an apparent typo '≤' and without proof) not recorded.
